newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian food trade deficit seen shrinking - paper.
newsitem.headline: Croatian food trade deficit seen shrinking - paper.

text.p: Croatia's trade deficit in food products could shrink by $40 million in 1996 as imports shrink, the daily Vecernji List said on Monday.
The deficit for the full year could fall to $380 million from $420 million in 1995, it said.
Quoting official statistics, the newspaper put the food product trade deficit at $306 million in January-October, down from some $350 million in the same period of 1995.
Food exports rose four percent, boosted by an 80 percent rise in sugar, while imports fell four percent, including a 12 percent drop in fruit imports, it said.
Uncontrolled food imports last year reached a record $929 million, angering farmers who staged a number of protests, forcing the government to introduce controls to protect domestic output.
The government is working on three separate laws to give better protection to farmers, but a shortage of funds could hamper a policy of subsidies, the paper said.
